displayName: Acme storefront cart/pricing (PHP → Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + JUnit 5)
description: Reference PHP → Java-21 / Spring Boot 3 scaffold for an Acme storefront cart/pricing slice, from a signed php spec (targetStack=java-spring). Demonstrates the PHP→static-type idiom gap end-to-end: loose == juggling ("0" == false) ⟶ explicit typed comparison; the PHP array-as-ordered-map ⟶ a CartLine record + Map; isset/empty/?? ⟶ Optional/nullable WITHOUT the empty("0") bug (a real 0 is preserved); the $_SESSION superglobal ⟶ an injected SessionCartPort; money-as-float ⟶ BigDecimal (HALF_UP, 2dp); and @-suppressed silent failures ⟶ explicit typed exceptions. Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj, no framework on the classpath); the Spring constructs are documented @TargetMapping contracts and the pure business logic is real Java the JUnit suite verifies. This is the Java option of a dual-target pair — dotnet8/canonical-php-catalog-service is the .NET 8 projection of the same signed spec, and the SME picks the target per routine.

matches.fallback: Used for php routines in a cart/pricing/checkout slice (loose comparisons, array shapes, superglobal state, money math, or @-suppressed error handling).

verification.sourceExecutionEquivalenceReason: PHP has a free/OSS runtime, so source-execution equivalence is FEASIBLE via a php-sidecar (run the source, compare outputs) — unlike ABL. That sidecar is not built yet, so equivalence is NOT claimed here.
